intro.quote: The protocol has been designed to be simple and flexible to allow parameter negotiation, and to minimize the number of round-trips.

steps.explain: The client sends its SSH identification string once the transport connection is established.

cite.quote: When the connection has been established, both sides MUST send an identification string.

steps.explain: The server sends its SSH identification string once the transport connection is established.

cite.quote: When the connection has been established, both sides MUST send an identification string.

steps.explain: The client begins algorithm negotiation by sending SSH_MSG_KEXINIT.

cite.quote: Key exchange begins by each side sending the following packet: byte SSH_MSG_KEXINIT

steps.explain: The server sends its own SSH_MSG_KEXINIT so both sides can select mutually supported algorithms.

cite.quote: Key exchange begins by each side sending the following packet: byte SSH_MSG_KEXINIT

steps.explain: The client sends its Diffie-Hellman public value e.

cite.quote: First, the client sends the following: byte SSH_MSG_KEXDH_INIT mpint e

steps.explain: The server returns its host key, Diffie-Hellman public value f, and a signature over the exchange hash.

cite.quote: The server then responds with the following: byte SSH_MSG_KEXDH_REPLY string server public host key and certificates (K_S) mpint f string signature of H

steps.explain: The client sends SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS to end key exchange and switch to the new keys.

cite.quote: Key exchange ends by each side sending an SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS message.

steps.explain: The server sends SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS to end key exchange and switch to the new keys.

cite.quote: Key exchange ends by each side sending an SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS message.

steps.explain: The client requests a named service after key exchange.
The server accepts the requested service when it supports the service and permits the client to use it.

cite.quote: If the server supports the service (and permits the client to use it), it MUST respond with the following: byte SSH_MSG_SERVICE_ACCEPT string service name

intro.quote: Either party MAY initiate the re-exchange, but roles MUST NOT be changed (i.e., the server remains the server, and the client remains the client).

steps.explain: The client initiates a key re-exchange by sending SSH_MSG_KEXINIT when no exchange is already in progress.

cite.quote: Key re-exchange is started by sending an SSH_MSG_KEXINIT packet when not already doing a key exchange (as described in Section 7.1).

steps.explain: The server responds with its own SSH_MSG_KEXINIT while retaining its server role.

cite.quote: When this message is received, a party MUST respond with its own SSH_MSG_KEXINIT message, except when the received SSH_MSG_KEXINIT already was a reply.

intro.quote: Each packet is in the following format:

fields.name: packet_length
fields.explain: This is the byte length of the packet, excluding the MAC and the packet_length field itself.

fields.name: padding_length
fields.explain: This gives the length in bytes of the random padding.

fields.name: payload
fields.explain: This contains the useful packet contents and is compressed when compression has been negotiated.

fields.name: random padding
fields.explain: This contains arbitrary-length padding used to align the encrypted packet.

fields.name: mac
fields.explain: This contains the Message Authentication Code when message authentication has been negotiated.

cite.quote: byte[m] mac (Message Authentication Code - MAC); m = mac_length

intro.quote: Key exchange begins by each side sending the following packet:

fields.name: SSH_MSG_KEXINIT
fields.explain: This identifies the message that begins key-exchange algorithm negotiation.

fields.name: cookie
fields.explain: This is a random value generated by the sender.

fields.name: kex_algorithms
fields.explain: This lists the supported key-exchange algorithms in preference order.

fields.name: server_host_key_algorithms
fields.explain: This lists acceptable algorithms for the server's host key.

fields.name: encryption_algorithms_client_to_server
fields.explain: This lists acceptable symmetric encryption algorithms for the client-to-server direction.

fields.name: encryption_algorithms_server_to_client
fields.explain: This lists acceptable symmetric encryption algorithms for the server-to-client direction.

fields.name: mac_algorithms_client_to_server
fields.explain: This lists acceptable MAC algorithms for the client-to-server direction.

fields.name: mac_algorithms_server_to_client
fields.explain: This lists acceptable MAC algorithms for the server-to-client direction.

fields.name: compression_algorithms_client_to_server
fields.explain: This lists acceptable compression algorithms for the client-to-server direction.

fields.name: compression_algorithms_server_to_client
fields.explain: This lists acceptable compression algorithms for the server-to-client direction.

fields.name: languages_client_to_server
fields.explain: This lists the client's preferred language tags in the client-to-server direction.

fields.name: languages_server_to_client
fields.explain: This lists the server's preferred language tags in the server-to-client direction.

fields.name: first_kex_packet_follows
fields.explain: This boolean indicates whether a guessed key-exchange packet follows the message.

fields.name: reserved for future extension
fields.explain: This reserved field is set to zero for future extension.
